title: Bonds to increase safety, security; repair schools, update classrooms
ballot_label: Caption: Bonds to increase safety, security; repair schools, update classrooms. Question: Shall District maintain its existing bond rate, issue bonds strengthening security, repairing aging schools, improving classrooms conditions, vocational training spaces? If the bonds are approved, they will be payable from taxes on property or property ownership that are not subject to the limits of sections 11 and 11b, Article XI of the Oregon Constitution. Summary: This measure is estimated to maintain the existing District bond levy rate, no increase estimated with passage. If passed, State provides $6,126,000 in matching funds. The North Clackamas School District seeks approval for the issuance of general obligation bonds in the principal amount of $245 million in bonds to finance capital costs.
summary: Referred by the district board. Would authorize $245 million in general obligation bonds for school security and safety upgrades, ventilation and cooling, roof and building repairs, vocational training spaces, athletic facilities and technology. The district estimates the bond levy rate would stay at about $2.37 per $1,000 of assessed value, and a state match of $6,126,000 depends on passage. A community oversight committee and regular audits are required.
yes_means: A yes vote authorizes North Clackamas School District to issue $245 million in general obligation bonds for school safety and security, building repairs, classroom and vocational-space updates.
no_means: A no vote does not authorize the bonds, and the district would not receive the $6,126,000 state matching funds.
fiscal_impact: Per the county pamphlet: $245 million in general obligation bonds, issued in series maturing within 21 years; because existing bonds are maturing, the measure is estimated to continue the current bond levy rate of about $2.37 per $1,000 of assessed value, with no increase. Actual rates may differ with interest rates and property values. The district would receive $6,126,000 in state matching funds only if the bond passes.

arguments.author: Simona Beattie, Community in Support of NC12
arguments.statement: Community in Support of NC12, in an argument signed by school board and budget committee members, says the bond addresses critical facility needs without increasing the current tax rate.
arguments.excerpt: Funds from this bond allow our district to address critical facility needs without increasing the current tax rate. That was by design.

arguments.author: Will Anderson, Milwaukie City Council President
arguments.statement: Milwaukie's mayor and city councilors, in an argument furnished by Council President Will Anderson, say the bond would fund heating, ventilation, cooling, security and other upgrades at every neighborhood school.
arguments.excerpt: Every school gets updates to heating, ventilation, and cooling systems, WiFi upgrades, new security cameras, and lockboxes for emergency responders.

arguments.author: Nicole Woodfill, Community in Support of NC12
arguments.statement: School parents and teachers, in an argument furnished by Community in Support of NC12, say the bond would address hot classrooms and aging systems without raising the current tax rate.
arguments.excerpt: Our teachers see firsthand how learning is affected when classrooms become too hot, aging systems fail, or facilities don’t meet students’ needs.

arguments.author: Nicole Woodfill, Community in Support of NC12
arguments.statement: An argument furnished by Community in Support of NC12 says the bond funds safety and security upgrades and accessibility improvements, including at Rex Putnam High School.
arguments.excerpt: The bond also funds meaningful investments in accessibility. Upgrades will improve access for students, families, and community members with disabilities, ensuring school buildings are welcoming and usable for everyone.

arguments.author: Nicole Woodfill, Community in Support of NC12
arguments.statement: An argument furnished by Community in Support of NC12 says well-maintained schools serve as community hubs and that the bond would fund repairs and cooling systems at no increase to the current tax rate.
arguments.excerpt: Well-maintained schools do more than just serve students. They are a beacon of our community, serving as hubs for events, activities, and services that connect neighbors and support families.
